artworks.title: Pandora
artworks.description: Waterhouse's Pre-Raphaelite Pandora kneels over the fatal casket in a wooded hollow — Hesiod's first woman as curious opener, the jar restyled as a Victorian box. The moment before the world's troubles spill.

artworks.title: Pandora
artworks.description: Rossetti's half-length Pandora holds the sealed box against a sulphurous glow — Jane Morris as the gift the gods sent to punish mankind. The Pre-Raphaelite jar made into a jewel of dread.

artworks.title: Eva Prima Pandora
artworks.description: Cousin's Louvre masterpiece fuses Eve and Pandora on one reclining nude — the first woman as both biblical fall and Hesiodic jar. Renaissance France's great allegory of curiosity and ruin.

artworks.title: Pandora
artworks.description: Lefebvre's academic Pandora stands with the box still closed — beauty as bait, the gift Zeus sent through Epimetheus. Salon mythology at full polish: the woman who has not yet opened the world.

popCulture.title: Pandora
popCulture.description: The jar (not box) that released evils remains the West's emblem of curiosity's cost — hope alone left under the lid.

popCulture.title: Pandora's box
popCulture.description: The English idiom for a gift that unleashes irreversible trouble — Hesiod's jar renamed a box by later translators and proverb makers.
